_doc: HMTc Category 18 (Pet Supplements) compiler config for tools/standards/compile-category.mjs. Method v2.0, DOUBLE OVER-COMPLIANCE form, sitting at the intersection of two live precedents. Category 17 (Pet Foods) established that animal-feed law is a disclosed FLOOR and never the certification value, and that pet products are certified to the strictest applicable HUMAN-food maximum. Category 16 (Dietary Supplements, human) established that a supplement is certified to the strictest CHILD-protective human-food maximum regardless of the labelled consumer, because concentrated dosage forms produce high body-weight-normalised intake in a small consumer. A pet supplement is both a pet product and a supplement, so Category 18 applies both rules: every numeric cell is a DISCLOSED READ-ACROSS to the strictest applicable AS-SOLD child-protective human-food sovereign maximum, and the three floors that legally govern or plausibly reach the cell — the EU complementary-feed-for-pet-animals and feed-additive limits under Directive 2002/32/EC and Regulation (EC) No 1831/2003, Japan's statutory Pet Food Safety Act maxima for lead, cadmium and inorganic arsenic under the FAMIC Specifications and Standards of Pet Food, and the human food-supplement maximum levels of the EU, Israel, Thailand, GSO, Vietnam, ASEAN and Singapore — are named on every cell and never select a number. No cell is a `gov` cell, because no sovereign regulates a pet supplement in the as-sold human-food basis this standard is written in; the honesty of saying so is the defensibility. No cell is occurrence-derived: the hyperaccumulator and adulteration histories recorded in the scope notes inform sampling posture and never a ceiling. Basis is never conflated: the row-level basis guard admits only register rows the register itself classifies as_sold, which mechanically selects the powder limb wherever a government instrument writes its own powder/liquid split and blocks every feed-basis and reconstituted-basis row; where the binding instrument is not form-split at all, as with Israel's food-for-special-dietary-purpose limb that anchors lead, cadmium and total mercury, the guard simply confirms the row is written on the product as placed on market. Allowed provenance tags: regulatory-alignment, read-across, not-material, control, ratchet. STAFF / HMTc content, not public wiki (CLAUDE.md Part 19 firewall).

_category.name: Pet Supplements
_category.anchor: No sovereign government sets a heavy-metal maximum for a pet supplement in a human-food basis. The instruments that reach the exact cell are pet-feed and animal-feed instruments. Japan's Pet Food Safety Act is the strongest of them: the FAMIC Specifications and Standards of Pet Food are statutory, pet-scoped and recorded on an as-sold basis, and they set lead at 3000, cadmium at 1000 and inorganic arsenic at 2000 ug/kg (jp_petfood_2021_pb_3000, jp_petfood_2021_cd_1000, jp_petfood_2021_ias_2000) and set nothing for the remaining panel analytes. The EU feed instruments follow (Directive 2002/32/EC complementary feed for pet animals, mineral feed and trace-element feed additives under Regulation (EC) No 1831/2003), then FDA CVM compliance policy — which is named for completeness because it is routinely cited as the US pet-food metals floor, but which the register carries no row for, so it is disclosed here as a described floor rather than a cited one and is recorded as a register gap — then China's pet-feed guidance, which is draft and gated out of the register in any event. NASC's quality guidelines are voluntary and non-binding and are not a sovereign source at all. Every one of these floors is one hundred to three hundred times looser than the corresponding value published here, and every one is named on the cell it reaches. HMTc treats the feed instruments as a disclosed floor and anchors every published cell on the strictest applicable AS-SOLD child-protective human-food sovereign maximum, following Category 17's human-grade over-compliance and Category 16's child-protective supplement rule together. Where no as-sold sovereign value exists in any jurisdiction (aluminium, total chromium, hexavalent chromium, methylmercury) the cell is a control: mandatory testing with a published method and escalation rule, and no invented ceiling.
_category.basis_family: as sold — the supplement as packaged and dosed (dry weight for powders, chews, tablets and capsules; neat liquid for oils and drops). No reconstitution, dilution, or as-fed conversion is performed anywhere in this category.
_category.method_label: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default), pet-supplement double over-compliance form: the exact cell's only sovereign maximum is an animal-feed instrument, which is disclosed as a floor and never used; every published value is a disclosed read-across to the strictest applicable as-sold child-protective human-food sovereign maximum in the product's native as-sold basis, or a control where no as-sold sovereign value exists. Never occurrence-derived.
_category.method_note:
Why the anchor family is child-protective rather than adult-supplement. The nearest same-form sovereign analog for a pet supplement is a human food supplement, and several governments do set maxima for those. HMTc does not use them, for the same reason Category 16 does not: they are an adult-intake framework, they run one to three orders of magnitude above the child-food ceilings, and a companion animal is a small-bodied consumer receiving a concentrated dose. A four-kilogram cat given a one-gram daily supplement scoop, or a five-kilogram dog given a soft chew, sits in a body-weight-normalised intake range comparable to an infant on formula and far above a seventy-kilogram adult. That is the disclosed rationale for which analog family HMTc adopts; it is not a calculation and it does not select any number. Every number still comes from a named sovereign instrument in the register, and the instrument, the limb of the instrument, and the floors HMTc declined are all named on the cell.

Why the numbers differ from HMTc Category 16 in three cells, and why two earlier divergences are now closed. Category 16 anchors its numeric cells on the liquid or ready-to-eat limb of form-split instruments and applies those values to as-sold solid supplements. Category 18 cannot do that: the register classifies those limbs as_consumed, the 8:1 powder-to-liquid conversion is confined to infant formula, and Method v2.0 step 4 requires preserving the product-form split the government rule itself writes. Two of the earlier divergences are now closed, and closed by finding a stricter as-sold instrument rather than by abandoning the basis rule. Cadmium and total mercury are anchored on Israel's food-for-special-dietary-purpose limb (il_fcs2016_cd_15_food_for_special_dietary_purpose_5 at 5 ug/kg, il_fcs2016_thg_16_food_for_special_dietary_purpose_4 at 4 ug/kg), which is not form-split and which matches Category 16's published values exactly; lead was already equal at 10 ug/kg and is now anchored on the same limb (il_fcs2016_pb_16_food_for_special_dietary_purpose_10). Three divergences remain, every one of them in the lax direction, and each is named here and again on its own cell. Inorganic arsenic: Category 16 reads eu2023_ias_formula_liquid_10 across at 10 ug/kg; Category 18 takes the powder limb eu2023_ias_formula_powder_20 at 20 ug/kg. Nickel: Category 16 reads eu2024_ni_formula_liquid_100 across at 100 ug/kg; Category 18 takes eu2024_ni_formula_powder_250 at 250 ug/kg. Aluminium: Category 16 reads aunz_sch19_al_formula_nonsoy_500 across at 500 ug/kg, describing it there as the only government aluminium maximum level for any food in any jurisdiction, while Category 18 declines that row because the register classifies it as_consumed ('portion ordinarily consumed') and no permitted conversion makes it comparable, and publishes a control with no ceiling at all — so a pet supplement certified here receives no numeric aluminium ceiling where a human supplement certified under Category 16 receives 500 ug/kg. In all three, the Category 18 basis reasoning is the more rigorous of the two and the Category 16 cell is the side performing an undisclosed as-consumed to as-sold read; the reconciliation is logged against Category 16 and is not performed from inside this config. The list is exhaustive and checkable cell by cell against the compiled records, and it names the direction of each difference rather than only its existence.

Why Israel's food-for-special-dietary-purpose limb anchors lead, cadmium and total mercury. Israel's FCS-2016 metal-contaminant table carries three limbs that could reach a purpose-formulated product: the infant and toddler formula limbs, the 'food for special dietary purpose' limb (Pb row 16 at 10, Cd row 15 at 5, tHg row 16 at 4), and a separate 'dietary supplements' limb (Pb row 17 at 3000, Cd row 16 at 1000, tHg row 15 at 100). The supplement limb is declined for the reason Category 16 declines every adult-supplement floor. That leaves the formula limbs and the special-dietary-purpose limb, both inside this category's declared analog family, and Method v2.0 step 3 then requires the strictest applicable of them, which is the special-dietary-purpose limb in all three cells. The determination is stated rather than assumed: HMTc is not applying Israel's own classification of a supplement, which would be the 3000/1000/100 limb, but Israel's strictest formulated-food ceiling, to a product Israel does not regulate at all. The full argument, with every declined limb named, sits on each of the three cells.

The two applicability filters, in order. The first is mechanical: only register rows the register itself classifies basis_class=as_sold may anchor a cell, which blocks every reconstituted and feed-basis row without any judgment being exercised. The second is declared and uniform: the anchor must come from the adopted analog family, which is finished foods intended for a small consumer. The second filter is needed because basis_class records whether a limit is written on the product as sold, not how much water the commodity contains, so a fresh-vegetable or fluid-milk ceiling can pass the mechanical filter and still be looser than it looks against an as-sold dry concentrate. The widened stricter-unselected audit scan is pointed at exactly those commodity families so that every such row surfaces in the derivation report with its disposition attached, rather than being quietly out of scope. The audit scope is now identical on all seven subcategories, so the scan is the same scan on every row and a disposition written on one row is true of that row rather than of the category in the abstract. It surfaces exactly one entry across the whole category: il_fcs2016_ias_1_milk_10, the Israeli fluid-milk inorganic-arsenic ceiling, on the inorganic-arsenic cell of all seven subcategories. It is not adopted. Every other row the earlier version of this category surfaced — hk_cap132v_thg_vegetables-other-than-edible-fungi_10, hk_cap132v_thg_milk_10, hk_cap132v_thg_secondary-milk-products_10, il_fcs2016_thg_1_milk_10 and il_fcs2016_cd_1_milk_5 — sits at or above the values now published for cadmium and total mercury and is therefore no longer stricter than any binding. A separate sweep is run outside this compiler with no scope regex, no infant exclusion and no reliance on basis_class tagging, counting a row as as-sold if its basis_class is as_sold or if its free-text basis carries the register's as-sold wording; it returns four further rows stricter than a binding in this category, and all four are packaged drinking-water ceilings: il_fcs2016_cd_17_bottled_drinking_water_and_mineral_water_3, il_fcs2016_tas_16_1_bottled_drinking_water_and_mineral_water_10, il_fcs2016_ias_16_1_bottled_drinking_water_and_mineral_water_6 and il_fcs2016_thg_17_bottled_drinking_water_and_mineral_water_1. Water is a different matrix consumed in litres per day rather than grams per dose, this category does not read a drinking-water ceiling across to a dosed concentrate, and each is named on its own cell. That is the whole set. The claim is deliberately stated in a form that can be falsified by re-running the sweep, rather than in a form that silently depends on a register tagging field being complete — the earlier version of this sentence rested on exactly that dependency and was wrong because of it.

Why all seven rows carry the same numbers. The adopted anchor family is a finished-child-food ceiling, which is defined by the consumer and the basis rather than by the ingredient, so it does not vary between a vitamin powder and a botanical blend. Category 16 publishes the same uniform shape for the same reason. The rows differ where the evidence actually differs: in the methylmercury posture (every-lot speciation where marine or freshwater material is routine, reflex speciation otherwise), in the hexavalent-chromium posture (every-lot speciation trigger where mineral, clay or geologic carriers are declared, and a lead-and-chromium co-elevation adulteration trigger on the botanical row), in the total-chromium rationale (chromium is a declared nutrient in the vitamin and mineral row and a contaminant everywhere else), and in the tin escalation rule. Occurrence history is recorded in the scope notes because it drives sampling posture; it never moves a ceiling.
_category.credible_note: The default credible-regulator set is widened by two national food-safety authorities, each because it is the only sovereign that regulates a cell the default set leaves empty, and in each case the addition makes the standard stricter rather than more convenient. India (FSSAI, Food Safety and Standards Regulations, Metal Contaminants) supplies the only as-sold child-food total-arsenic maximum and the only as-sold non-canned child-food tin maximum; no EU, UK, Codex, US, Canadian or FSANZ instrument sets either. Israel (Ministry of Health, Food Control Services, FCS-2016) supplies the only as-sold child-food total-mercury maximum in any jurisdiction — the EU, UK, Codex, US, Canadian and FSANZ child-food instruments set no mercury maximum at all — and its 'food for special dietary purpose' limb additionally supplies the strictest as-sold sovereign lead, cadmium and total-mercury ceilings on the register for a purpose-formulated finished food, which is why Israel now anchors three of this category's seven numeric cells rather than one. Each of those three adoptions moves the published value down or holds it level; none makes the standard more convenient. Both are binding national maximum levels enforced by a sovereign food authority, both are already relied on by the live HMTc human-supplement standard (Category 16), and Israel's FCS-2016 is already relied on by the live Category 25 standard. Widening the set also widens this compiler's stricter-unselected audit scan to Indian and Israeli rows, so the addition increases audit coverage as well as strictness.

pet-supplements-vitamin-mineral.name: Vitamin/mineral supplements
pet-supplements-vitamin-mineral.native_basis_label: the supplement as sold (as-packaged concentrate) — dry weight for powders, chews, tablets and capsules, neat liquid for oils and drops; no reconstitution, dilution, or as-fed conversion is applied
pet-supplements-vitamin-mineral.scope_note: Single-nutrient and multi-nutrient vitamin and mineral supplements for companion animals, in any as-sold dosage form (powder, tablet, capsule, soft chew, paste, liquid drop). This is the row where inorganic raw materials dominate: mineral salts and carbonates, trace-mineral concentrates, marine-derived mineral sources such as calcified seaweed, and clay, zeolite or diatomaceous-earth carriers and anti-caking agents are all recognised lead, cadmium and arsenic routes, and the ceilings below are held at full strictness for that reason rather than relaxed toward occurrence. Chromium may be a declared nutrient in this row, which is why total chromium is a control and hexavalent chromium is the species that binds. Boundary rules from the HMTc taxonomy govern placement: the product must be intended for animal consumption as a supplement rather than as the sole or primary diet; anything bearing an AAFCO nutritional adequacy statement routes to Category 17 (Pet Foods); and a dental chew routes to Category 17 (pet chews), because its primary function is food or treat rather than supplementation.
pet-supplements-vitamin-mineral.basis_guard: as sold|as_sold|as-sold|product as placed on (the )?market|as prepared for (wholesale|retail|consum)|finished product|by weight|dry weight|neat liquid|product as offered to consumer
pet-supplements-vitamin-mineral.basis_guard_note: Every named anchor must be a register row the register itself classifies basis_class=as_sold. A pet supplement is dosed as sold: a scoop of powder, a chew, a capsule, a pump of neat oil. It is never reconstituted, and the 8:1 powder-to-liquid conversion is confined to infant formula (CLAUDE.md Part 19), so no conversion is available to make a ready-to-feed liquid maximum comparable to an as-sold concentrate. The guard therefore blocks (a) every liquid/ready-to-feed limb of a form-split infant instrument, which the register classifies as_consumed, (b) the AU-NZ Schedule 19 'portion ordinarily consumed' rows, and (c) every animal-feed instrument, whose basis is a 12%-moisture feed basis with no as_sold classification. Where a government instrument writes its own powder/liquid split and that instrument supplies the binding anchor, the guard mechanically selects the powder limb, which is what Method v2.0 step 4 requires: preserve the product-form split the government rule itself writes. That is the position on inorganic arsenic (EU 2023/915) and nickel (EU 2024/1987), the two cells where a form-split instrument still binds. It is not the position on lead, cadmium and total mercury: those three are anchored on Israel's FCS-2016 food-for-special-dietary-purpose limb, which is not form-split at all, so on those cells the guard does no limb selection and only confirms the row is written on the product as placed on market. Choosing the stricter liquid limb for an as-sold concentrate would be a silent basis conversion in the strict direction, which is still a conflation, and the as-consumed limbs declined on that ground are named cell by cell. 2026-09-02: the guard previously matched only the literal token as_sold (a native_basis label, not register basis text), so no in-force row could ever pass it; widened to the as-sold basis family.

read_across.label: Child-protective, human-grade read-across to the FSSAI total-arsenic maximum for infant milk substitute and infant foods, which the register records on an as-sold basis (the source column is parts per million by weight with no reconstitution basis stated). Total arsenic is a total-element cell in its own right and additionally gates the inorganic-arsenic speciation reflex; the toxic species is limited separately.
read_across.substantiation: No regulator in the default credible set sets a total-arsenic maximum for any child food: the EU, UK, Codex, US, Canadian and FSANZ instruments regulate inorganic arsenic only. The as-sold sovereign child-food total-arsenic rows are FSSAI (the strictest, adopted here), the Singapore Food Agency baby-food and infant-formula rows (sg_foodregs_2026_baby_food_tas_100, sg_foodregs_2026_infant_formula_tas_100), a Chinese milk-powder row and the Israeli formula-powder row (il_fcs2016_tas_14_1_infant_and_toddler_formulas_powder_1000). FSSAI is admitted to this category's credible-regulator set for that reason and it makes the standard stricter, not more convenient. The animal-feed floor that legally governs this cell is disclosed and never used: in the EU a pet supplement is complementary feed for pet animals or a feed additive under Directive 2002/32/EC and Regulation (EC) No 1831/2003 (register rows eu2002_32_pb_complementary_feed_10000, eu2002_32_cd_pet_complementary_feed_2000, eu2002_32_tas_complementary_feed_4000, eu2002_32_thg_mineral_feed_200, eu2002_32_pb_mineral_feed_15000, eu2002_32_cd_mineral_feed_materials_2000, eu2002_32_tas_mineral_feed_12000 and the trace-element and binder/anti-caking additive rows), with China's draft pet-feed guidance in the same range. Japan's Pet Food Safety Act is disclosed on the same footing and is the one pet-scoped floor that is neither draft nor guidance: the FAMIC Specifications and Standards of Pet Food set statutory maxima that the register records on an as-sold basis for lead, cadmium and inorganic arsenic only (jp_petfood_2021_pb_3000, jp_petfood_2021_cd_1000, jp_petfood_2021_ias_2000), and set nothing for the remaining panel analytes. Category 17, the live pet-foods standard this category builds on, names the same three rows, and Category 18 names them here for the same reason. They run one hundred to three hundred times above the corresponding values published in this category. They are outside this compiler's audit scan because Japan sits outside this category's credible-regulator set, not because any basis mechanism blocks them; the honest statement is that HMTc declines them as a floor, not that the machinery could not see them. The human food-supplement floor (eu2023_cd_food_supplements_1000, th_moph414_2020_pb_food_supplement_1000, il_fcs2016_pb_17_dietary_supplements_3000, il_fcs2016_cd_16_dietary_supplements_except_listed_categories_1000, il_fcs2016_thg_15_dietary_supplements_100, gso193_2021_thg_food_supplements_100, asean2017_pb_health_supplements_10000, hsa2024_pb_health_supplements_10000) is likewise disclosed and never used. Of the three floors, only the EU feed rows are unreachable by construction: they carry a 12%-moisture feed basis with no as_sold classification, so this row's basis guard blocks them and the audit scan drops any row whose basis names feed. The human food-supplement rows are not blocked by any mechanism at all — Israel's supplement rows are classified as-sold and match this row's audit scope — so they are declined by the declared analog-family filter alone, which is exactly why that filter is stated openly in _category.method_note instead of being left to the machinery to enforce silently. Register-tagging note for this cell, recorded because this cell's defensibility turns on the basis field. The FSSAI row's free-text basis previously read 'as consumed' while its basis_class read as_sold and its own notes recorded the as-sold correction against the FSSAI 2011 primary text, whose column header is parts per million by weight with no reconstitution basis stated — a half-applied correction that left the human-readable field contradicting the machine-readable one. The basis field now reads 'as sold', matching its already-corrected sibling in_sn_infant-milk-substitute-and-infant-foods_5000, and the same correction has been applied to the two other FSSAI Metal Contaminants infant rows that carried it (in_pb_infant-milk-substitute-and-infant-foods_200, in_cd_infant-milk-substitute-and-infant-foods_100). No value, scope or basis_class changed. The independent as-sold sweep returns one credible row stricter than this binding, il_fcs2016_tas_16_1_bottled_drinking_water_and_mineral_water_10, a packaged drinking-water ceiling in a different matrix; it is not adopted.

The rice-specific child-food rows (fda2020_ias_infant_rice_cereal_100, us_ias_rice-cereals-for-infants-all-types-white_100, ca_ias_rice-based-foods-intended-specifically-f_100, uk_ias_rice-destined-for-the-production-of-food_100) are laxer and commodity-scoped. Rice-derived carriers (rice maltodextrin, rice flour, rice hull) are a recognised inorganic-arsenic route into supplement dosage forms and are held to this ceiling, not to the rice-commodity ceiling. The human food-supplement floor (eu2023_cd_food_supplements_1000, th_moph414_2020_pb_food_supplement_1000, il_fcs2016_pb_17_dietary_supplements_3000, il_fcs2016_cd_16_dietary_supplements_except_listed_categories_1000, il_fcs2016_thg_15_dietary_supplements_100, gso193_2021_thg_food_supplements_100, asean2017_pb_health_supplements_10000, hsa2024_pb_health_supplements_10000) is likewise disclosed and never used. The human food-supplement rows are not blocked by any mechanism at all — Israel's supplement rows are classified as-sold and match this row's audit scope — so they are declined by the declared analog-family filter alone, which is exactly why that filter is stated openly in _category.method_note instead of being left to the machinery to enforce silently. Divergence from HMTc Category 16, disclosed. Category 16 anchors inorganic arsenic on eu2023_ias_formula_liquid_10 and publishes 10 ug/kg for as-sold solid supplements; Category 18 declines that row because the register classifies it as_consumed, and reads the powder limb of the same instrument at 20 ug/kg instead. This category publishes the laxer of the two numbers and says so. The reason is the basis rule rather than a policy preference, and no stricter as-sold sovereign inorganic-arsenic instrument exists anywhere in the credible set for a non-water, non-fluid-commodity matrix, so there is nothing available to close the gap without performing the conversion Method v2.0 forbids. The reconciliation belongs on the Category 16 side and is logged with the aluminium item.

read_across.label: Child-protective, human-grade read-across to the powder limb of the EU 2024/1987 nickel maximum for infant and young-child formula placed on the market as powder, except soy protein isolate — the strictest as-sold sovereign nickel ceiling for a dry child-food concentrate.
read_across.substantiation: EU 2024/1987 is the only instrument in any jurisdiction that sets nickel maxima for food, and it writes its own powder/liquid and soy/non-soy splits. The powder limb is the applicable limb for an as-sold concentrate; the liquid limb (eu2024_ni_formula_liquid_100) is classified as_consumed and governs ready-to-feed liquid. The soy powder limb (eu2024_ni_formula_soy_powder_400), the baby-food limb (eu2024_ni_babyfood_500) and the processed-cereal limb (eu2024_ni_processed_cereal_babyfood_3000) are all laxer, so the non-soy powder limb is the strictest applicable as-sold value. They are outside this compiler's audit scan because Japan sits outside this category's credible-regulator set, not because any basis mechanism blocks them; the honest statement is that HMTc declines them as a floor, not that the machinery could not see them. The human food-supplement floor (eu2023_cd_food_supplements_1000, th_moph414_2020_pb_food_supplement_1000, il_fcs2016_pb_17_dietary_supplements_3000, il_fcs2016_cd_16_dietary_supplements_except_listed_categories_1000, il_fcs2016_thg_15_dietary_supplements_100, gso193_2021_thg_food_supplements_100, asean2017_pb_health_supplements_10000, hsa2024_pb_health_supplements_10000) is likewise disclosed and never used. Of the three floors, only the EU feed rows are unreachable by construction: they carry a 12%-moisture feed basis with no as_sold classification, so this row's basis guard blocks them and the audit scan drops any row whose basis names feed. The human food-supplement rows are not blocked by any mechanism at all — Israel's supplement rows are classified as-sold and match this row's audit scope — so they are declined by the declared analog-family filter alone, which is exactly why that filter is stated openly in _category.method_note instead of being left to the machinery to enforce silently.

Sn.basis_label: the supplement as sold (as-packaged concentrate) — dry weight for powders, chews, tablets and capsules, neat liquid for oils and drops; no reconstitution, dilution, or as-fed conversion is applied
Sn.binding_control: Container class is a certification precondition on this cell, not a variable ceiling. The published tin value governs every lot certified under Category 18 without exception. Tin-coated or otherwise unlacquered metal-can primary packaging is out of scope for this row; no alternate canned limb is offered, and eu2023_sn_canned_infant_formula_50000 and eu2023_sn_canned_foods_200000 are expressly excluded as substitute ceilings. Any quantifiable tin on a non-canned lot is treated as a packaging or contact-material finding and triggers a container investigation before release.

control.rationale: No government anywhere sets an aluminium contaminant maximum for a food on an as-sold basis. The only sovereign food aluminium numbers on the register are the FSANZ Schedule 19 infant-formula rows — aunz_sch19_al_formula_nonsoy_500 at 500 ug/kg for non-soy infant, follow-on and special-medical-purpose formula, and aunz_sch19_al_formula_soy_1000 at 1000 ug/kg for soy-based formula — which are written on a 'portion ordinarily consumed' reconstituted basis the register classifies as_consumed and which no permitted conversion makes comparable to an as-sold concentrate, and the Chinese GB 2760 baked-goods and starch-noodle rows, which are permitted food-additive residue allowances for alum firming and leavening agents rather than contaminant ceilings. The remaining aluminium rows are drinking-water guideline values and a plastics food-contact specific migration limit, both different matrices in different bases. Adopting the reconstituted FSANZ value for an as-sold powder would be a silent eight-fold basis conversion in the strict direction; adopting an additive-residue allowance as a contaminant ceiling would misdescribe the instrument. Neither is supportable, so no number is invented and testing is mandatory instead. This is the same disposition HMTc Category 17 publishes for aluminium in pet foods. Divergence from HMTc Category 16, disclosed here because this is the one cell where Category 18 publishes no ceiling and the live human-supplement standard publishes one. Category 16 reads aunz_sch19_al_formula_nonsoy_500 across to as-sold solid supplements and publishes 500 ug/kg, describing it there as the only government aluminium maximum level for any food in any jurisdiction. Category 18 declines the same row on basis grounds, and the consequence is stated plainly rather than left to be discovered: a pet supplement certified under Category 18 receives no numeric aluminium ceiling, only mandatory measurement and a trend control, where a human supplement certified under Category 16 receives 500 ug/kg. Category 18's basis reasoning is the more rigorous of the two, and the reconciliation belongs on the Category 16 side, which is the side performing an undisclosed as-consumed to as-sold read; it is logged for that purpose and is not resolved from inside this config.
control.reference_method: Total aluminium on every lot by ICP-MS after closed-vessel microwave acid digestion. Results are trended per SKU and per raw-material lot; a step change against the SKU's own established baseline, or any result attributable to a declared aluminium-bearing processing aid, anti-caking agent, colour lake or clay/zeolite carrier, triggers a formulation and raw-material investigation before release. Aluminium results are reported on the certificate rather than suppressed.
